gags.name: Barack Obama Secret Vote Joke
gags.summary: Characters make jokes about publicly supporting Barack Obama while privately undermining that support, satirising liberal hypocrisy.

gags.name: Mickey Rourke Non Sequiturs
gags.summary: Characters drop bizarrely specific and increasingly absurd references to Mickey Rourke in unrelated situations.

best.text: 'But you made the same mistake Mickey Rourke made on that catamaran. You didn't kill me when you had the chance.'

gags.name: World's Greatest [Absurd Thing]
gags.summary: Characters bestow the title 'world's greatest' on increasingly ridiculous and implausible things or people.

best.text: I believe the moon doesn't exist. I believe that vampires are the world's greatest golfers, but their curse is that they'll never get to prove it. I believe that there are 31 letters in the white alphabet.

gags.name: Harvard Business School Brag
gags.summary: Jack repeatedly invokes his Harvard Business School credentials as self-important justification for his opinions and decisions.

best.text: Jack was voted 'most' at Harvard Business School.

gags.name: The Rural Juror

gags.name: Princess Leia Costume
gags.summary: Liz's Princess Leia costume recurs as a go-to outfit that immediately marks her as a hopeless nerd.

best.title: Believe in the Stars
best.text: 'I wear my Princess Leia costume and they dismiss me immediately.'

gags.name: Honky Grandma Be Trippin'
gags.summary: Tracy's signature film catchphrase that keeps resurfacing as shorthand for his lowbrow movie career.

best.title: The Break-Up
best.text: Hunky Grandma Be Trippin' made $96 million.

gags.name: Product Placement Acknowledgment
gags.summary: The show self-consciously calls attention to its own product placement deals, treating them as a running meta-joke.

best.title: The Ones
best.text: 'It's not product placement. I just like it.'

gags.name: You'll Be Back
gags.summary: Characters confidently tell someone who is leaving or threatening to leave forever that they will inevitably return.

best.text: If I ever see you again, I'll kill you. / Please. You'll be back.

gags.name: Liz's Muffin Top Song

gags.name: Three Different [Places]
gags.summary: Characters casually reveal they've done something absurd or extreme 'in three different' locations as if it were ordinary.

best.text: 'Having been shot and left for dead in three different deserts, pro-gun control.'

gags.name: Goodbye Forever
gags.summary: Characters dramatically declare 'goodbye forever' in departures that are never actually permanent.

best.title: Last Lunch

gags.name: Dr. Spaceman's Non Sequitur Responses
gags.summary: Dr. Spaceman responds to mundane statements with hilariously wrong or clueless corrections, revealing his incompetence.

gags.name: Shut It Down
gags.summary: Jack or others dramatically declare 'shut it down' to cancel something, often with absurd finality.

best.text: I'm gonna shut it down, leave it vacant, open the windows, and let nature have at it.

gags.name: "I've made a huge mistake"
gags.summary: Various characters, most often Michael and Gob, solemnly deliver the line "I've made a huge mistake" after realising the consequences of their latest bad decision.

best.text: I've made a huge mistake. [Michael, alone, after realizing Gob is keeping Marta]

gags.name: Buster's hook hand

best.text: [On the Next] 'Loose seal! Watch out for loose seal!' / 'I don't care about Lucille! She lies!' / Narrator: 'And then a seal bites off his hand.'

gags.name: "On the next Arrested Development"
gags.summary: Post-credits tags tease absurd, often non-canonical follow-up scenes that pay off earlier gags or introduce new ridiculous complications.

best.title: The Fallout

'Hey, gang, does Buster's mannequin look like...' / 'Judy Garland.' / 'Is it Lucille 2?' / 'Why is she smiling?' / 'This isn't a mannequin.' / '...' / 'This is... the happiest corpse I've ever seen.'

gags.name: Gob's magic act
gags.summary: Gob insists his performances are "illusions, not tricks," and his elaborate magic acts invariably go catastrophically wrong, often involving fire, animals, or an unwilling audience.

best.title: Pilot

best.title: A New Start
best.text: Looks like we got ourselves an Anus Tart.

gags.name: Opening narration variation
gags.summary: The show's opening narrator card is repeatedly remixed to swap in a different family member's name as the focal character, turning the premise itself into a running joke.

the one son who had no choice but to keep himself together
whose future was abruptly canceled and the one

best.text: Title card: 'Now the story of a family whose future was abruptly canceled and the one son-in-law who had no choice but to keep himself together. It's Tobias' Arrested Development.'

gags.summary: Lucille Bluth invented Cinco de Cuatro, a holiday on the fourth of May, specifically to spite Mexican-Americans by pre-empting their Cinco de Mayo celebration.

best.text: a particularly vicious response by a young Lucille Bluth to the Mexican holiday of Cinco de Mayo

gags.name: No touching / Touching
gags.summary: Prison guards shout "no touching" whenever inmates and visitors make physical contact, and the rule is gleefully violated and enforced as a recurring bit throughout prison visit scenes.

best.text: Prison guard: 'No touching.' — interrupting George Sr. and Buster's emotional moment

gags.name: Fakeblock privacy software
gags.summary: George Michael's supposed privacy software Fakeblock is entirely fake, yet everyone around him, investors, the press, Ron Howard, takes it completely seriously, escalating the deception across multiple episodes.
phrases: how does your privacy software work

best.text: Oh, my goodness. Fakeblock is so impressive. / Yeah. / I mean, Fakeblock's incredible. / Fakeblock is... / Yeah, Fakeblock is real.

gags.name: "There's always money in the banana stand"
gags.summary: George Sr.'s cryptic catchphrase about the banana stand turns out to be literally true, money is hidden in the walls, and the gag recurs whenever someone burns, destroys, or dismisses the stand.
phrases: there's always money in the banana stand

best.title: Development Arrested
best.text: Because my grandfather vowed one day he would get even for banana stand you stole from him.

gags.name: Abbi's full name as battle cry

gags.name: New York City love declarations

phrases: i love living in new york city

best.text: 'God, I love living in New York City. You just... You can't beat it. You get to be physically near the cutting edge of art and culture and then, just a mere decade later, actually afford to experience it.'

gags.name: white dudes commentary
gags.summary: Ilana repeatedly makes sweeping, exasperated pronouncements about white dudes as a monolithic force of mediocrity and fading power.

best.title: Citizen Ship
best.text: Ilana: 'Jaime, those old white dudes are impossible to tell apart.'

gags.name: Abbi has no upper body strength

gags.name: Drew Barrymore's bag

gags.name: I'm Rich, Biatch!
gags.summary: Chappelle's recurring sign-off catchphrase delivered with a celebratory horn honk.

best.title: Slavery Reparations
best.text: (Chappelle) I'm rich, biatch! (horn honking)

gags.name: Jim Belushi as a Unit of Mediocrity
gags.summary: Characters use Jim Belushi as a recurring metaphor for something that is bafflingly mediocre yet inexplicably persistent.

best.text: Sounds delicious. / I'm the center slice of a square pizza. You're Jim Belushi.

phrases: slept with the great eartha kitt

best.title: Competitive Ecology

gags.name: Annie's Boobs (the Monkey)
gags.summary: Troy's pet monkey named Annie's Boobs becomes a recurring joke, often addressed directly in deadpan asides.

gags.name: Caring About Six People
gags.summary: The number six recurs as a running joke tied to the study group's size, most pointedly in the line about caring about six people being a horrifying nightmare.

best.title: Basic Story
best.text: For the final stage of my appraisal, I'm gonna randomly select one of your vending machines to see if it can be rocked using human strength enough to tip and crush me. In the U.S., each year, six people die this way, and five of them are insurance appraisers, so I take this very seriously.

gags.name: Moist Towelette Empire
gags.summary: A recurring absurd callback to Pierce's family fortune being built on moist towelettes, played for comedy through its mundane unglamourousness.

best.title: Pillows and Blankets (2)
best.text: The dried-up heir to a moist towelette empire who would prove to be the dried-up heir to a moist towelette empire.

best.text: "Maybe Leonard was watching from the bushes and told Abed about it." / "I don't have cable."

gags.name: Wanna Watch (Movie Night)
gags.summary: Characters casually proposing to watch a film together recurs as a comedic beat, often with Abed as the instigator and the offer played for unexpected emotional weight or absurdity.

best.title: The Science of Illusion
best.text: Now, that was really funny. / What's going on? Where are the cameras? / Oh, we're not filming this. / No. Who'd wanna watch this?

gags.name: Cougar Town References

gags.name: You've Earned It
gags.summary: Characters solemnly bestow a privilege or title on someone with the phrase 'you've earned it', played as an absurdly grandiose reward for trivial things.

gags.name: Pretty Pretty Pretty Good

phrases: this dream brought to you by

phrases: it's probably not even my name legally anymore

best.text: Ben: 'Pizza? Never heard of it. That's what people will be saying in 20 years. Because pizza is old news, Chris. Pizza is your grandfather's calzone.'

gags.name: Dr. Richard Nygard
gags.summary: Chris Traeger constantly references his therapist Dr. Richard Nygard, with the joke escalating to him seeing the therapist an impossible number of times per week.
phrases: i see him fifteen times a week

first.title: How A Bill Becomes A Law

best.title: Pawnee Commons
best.text: Chris's talking-head: 'My therapist, Dr. Richard Nygard, suggested that I try some non-exercise-based hobbies. So I've been studying woodworking with Ron. I made this.' [shows something] 'Before I started, it was bigger.'

gags.name: Chris Traeger's superhuman health
gags.summary: Chris Traeger's body is treated as a medical marvel, with an absurdly low resting heart rate and physical stats that baffle scientists, used as a recurring joke about his extreme wellness obsession.

best.title: The Trial Of Leslie Knope
best.text: The transcript ends with: 'Mr. Traeger: That was beautiful. I'm literally crying and jumping. Crying noise, crying noise, nose blow. Mr. Wyatt: It's gonna be okay. Mr. Traeger: ...' [Oh.]

gags.name: JJ's Diner waffles
gags.summary: JJ's Diner and its waffles are treated as a sacred Pawnee institution, with Leslie and others referencing it with reverent affection as the pinnacle of breakfast food.
phrases: four horse meals of the egg-pork-alypse

best.title: Time Capsule
best.text: four horse meals of the egg-pork-alypse.

gags.name: Paunch Burger's grotesque portions
gags.summary: Paunch Burger serves comically oversized and unhealthy food, with portion sizes so large they're marketed as normal, used to satirize Pawnee's culture of excess.

best.title: Two Parties
best.text: Aw, sweet! A new Paunch Burger. Their burgers will kill you! They're full of wasps! Yeah, but they taste real good. Yes, they do, sir.

gags.name: Entertainment 720
gags.summary: Tom and Jean-Ralphio's ludicrously over-the-top media company that spends enormous sums on branding and parties while generating no revenue, eventually going bankrupt.

best.title: Meet N Greet
best.text: They say you've got to spend money to make money. Well, I don't know where we went wrong. We spent all of our money.

gags.name: Jerry / Larry / Garry's name
gags.summary: The parks department employee's name is perpetually wrong, called Jerry, then Larry, then Terry, then Garry, and no one ever settles on the right one, including the audience.

best.title: Two Funerals
best.text: Garry's first act as mayor: he starts crying at the podium, finally says 'I'm flying!' while overcome with emotion

gags.name: Moira's Sunrise Bay past
gags.summary: Moira's melodramatic soap opera past on Sunrise Bay is repeatedly invoked as a real reference point for life experience, blurring her identity with her character.

best.title: Love Letters
best.text: It was that week on 'Sunrise Bay' when Vivian Blake had her accident, you were in a body cast, they wouldn't let you take it off. You were writing with your left hand! / The spelunking incident. / No. It was after she got thrown upwards through a skylight.

gags.name: David's elaborate plans
gags.summary: David constructs needlessly over-engineered, theatrical plans for ordinary moments, engagements, announcements, store events, which inevitably go sideways or get mocked.

best.title: Life Is A Cabaret
best.text: David's elaborate, hyper-choreographed engagement announcement plan — dimming lights, popping bubbly, a speech, Alexis getting misty, a 'ripple effect of sobbing,' and Patrick's role is just to top up drinks.

gags.name: Crows movie saga
gags.summary: Moira's low-budget horror film The Crows Have Eyes keeps resurfacing as a running source of pride, embarrassment, and plot complications for the Rose family.

best.title: Meet The Parents
best.text: How did it end again? Like, a crowmageddon? / Crowpocalypse. But you didn't hear it from me.

gags.name: David's "very dark" inner life
gags.summary: Characters repeatedly react with alarmed laughter when David's offhand remarks or past behaviour reveal an unexpectedly bleak or disturbing inner world.

best.title: Love Letters
best.text: You've never written in a journal, have you? / No, but um, one time I did do a book report on David's diary, and it was very dark. Okay.

gags.name: Body milk
gags.summary: David's Rose Apothecary product 'body milk' keeps coming up as a running joke about the pretentiousness of the store's branding and David's inability to explain it sensibly.

best.title: Stop Saying Lice!
best.text: What do we think body milk is, if not milk for your body?!

gags.name: "In a ___ sort of way"
gags.summary: Characters, particularly the Roses, soften backhanded observations by appending "in a ___ sort of way," turning an insult into a strained compliment.
phrases: in a war-torn sort of way
in a homeless-y sort of way

best.title: Merry Christmas, Johnny Rose
best.text: W... I, for one, find it charming, in sort of a... a war-torn sort of way.

gags.name: Moira's tortured parental speeches
gags.summary: Whenever Moira attempts a sincere parental or public address she derails it with florid vocabulary and theatrical detours until someone (usually Johnny) urges her to get to the point.

best.title: Happy Anniversary
best.text: Moira's speech: 'Do you know your father and I hold great affection for the two of you? It may not always be obvious, but—' — Johnny: 'Just say it, Moira!'

gags.name: Blouse Barn
gags.summary: The Blouse Barn is repeatedly name-dropped as the town's comically unglamorous clothing store, used as a punchline about how far the Roses have fallen.

best.title: Turkey Shoot
best.text: Or one of your fashion-y blouses shrinks in the dryer, and you'll have to go to Janine's or get a shirt at the Blouse Barn, just like the rest of us.

gags.name: Alexis didn't finish high school
gags.summary: The fact that Alexis never finished high school is repeatedly brought up as a punchline, usually paired with an absurd exotic excuse involving celebrities, yachts, or drugs.
phrases: i did not finish high school

best.title: General Store
best.text: So as Jocelyn said, my name is Alexis, and yes, I did not finish high school. Um, it's this long, boring story involving a yacht, and a famous soccer player, and like... a ton of mushrooms.

gags.name: Community service couture
gags.summary: Moira treats her court-ordered community service as a glamorous public appearance, dressing in designer clothes and citing celebrity precedents like Naomi Campbell.

best.title: Wine And Roses
best.text: Naomi Campbell wore Dolce & Gabbana couture to her community service. And just because she was picking up roadkill did not mean that she needed to look like it. And I just always really admired her courage.

gags.name: "Who's to say?"
gags.summary: Characters, especially Stevie, deploy "who's to say?" as a breezy deflection whenever confronted with an inconvenient truth or a question they don't want to answer.

best.title: Happy Anniversary
best.text: Stevie reveals she kissed Jake: 'I kissed him too.' — David: 'Well, that didn't happen.' Stevie: 'Who's to say?'

gags.name: The whole family erupts
gags.summary: Small personal victories, a bike ride, a voicemail, an announcement, trigger a disproportionately joyful eruption from the entire Rose family gathered together.

best.title: Estate Sale
best.text: David successfully rides the bike — the whole family (and Stevie) erupting in celebration

gags.name: "That's not necessary"
gags.summary: Characters reflexively say "that's not necessary" to deflect offers of help or generosity, often immediately contradicted by their obvious need or desire for exactly what was offered.

best.title: Dead Guy In Room 4
best.text: Moira asks for 'a tea,' David says 'we don't sell tea,' Patrick offers to make a run to the café — Moira: 'No, that's not necessary. How serendipitous. Thank you, Peter.'

gags.name: McKigney the hand model cautionary tale
gags.summary: The story of doomed hand model Ray McKigney, who overused his hands and ended up with a frozen claw, dependent on Cub Scouts to feed him, is repeatedly invoked as a warning.
phrases: mckigney had a few good years

best.title: The Puffy Shirt
best.text: Towards the end, his hands became so frozen he was unable to manipulate utensils and was dependent on Cub Scouts to feed him.

gags.name: buffer zone
gags.summary: Characters use the term 'buffer zone' to describe the uncomfortable collapse of physical or social distance between themselves and someone they want to avoid.

best.title: The Shower Head
best.text: My buffer zone just went from 1200 miles down to two feet.

gags.name: The Tonight Show appearances
gags.summary: Jerry's Tonight Show appearances and the social fallout from them recur as a running comic backdrop, with characters offering unsolicited critiques of his performance.

best.title: The Shower Head
best.text: [Tonight Show interview] My family's nuts. They're crazy. My Uncle Leo, I had lunch with him the other day. He's one of these guys that anything goes wrong, he blames anti-Semitism. Know what I mean? The spaghetti's not al dente? Cook, anti-Semite. Loses a bet on a horse? Secretariat, anti-Semitic.

gags.name: Jerry's closing stand-up
gags.summary: Each episode ends with Jerry performing a stand-up bit that ties thematically back to the episode's events.

best.title: The Limo
best.text: Jerry's closing stand-up: Nazis in WWII movies have two separate 'Heils' — one formal, one casual office Heil

gags.name: low-talker
gags.summary: Characters encounter people who speak so quietly they can't be heard, leading to accidental agreements and misunderstandings.

best.title: The Glasses
best.text: Did you hear that? / That I heard.

gags.name: George's answering machine song
gags.summary: George records his answering machine greeting as a sung parody of the Greatest American Hero theme, to everyone's embarrassment.
phrases: believe it or not george isn't at home
believe it or not i'm not home

best.title: The Caddy
best.text: Frank Costanza's answering machine message, played while Steinbrenner is still in the room: 'I'm not here. Leave a message.' Then: 'Jerry, it's Frank Costanza. Mr. Steinbrenner's here. George is dead. Call me back.'

gags.name: Morty's beltless trenchcoat origin story
gags.summary: Morty Seinfeld repeatedly retells the story of how tripping over Jerry's toy one night inspired him to invent the Executive, his signature beltless trenchcoat.

best.title: The Raincoats (1)
best.text: I came home one night, and I tripped over one of Jerry's toys. So I took out my belt, just to threaten him, and I got a glimpse of myself in the mirror. That night, I cut off the loops, and the Executive was born.

gags.name: Del Boca Vista
gags.summary: Jerry's parents keep moving to and causing drama at the Del Boca Vista retirement community in Florida.

best.title: The Cadillac (2)
best.text: I'm free! Where are they moving to? / Del Boca Vista! / That's where my parents are gonna live. We can visit together. / I know. / Every five years!

gags.name: What kind of a sick person
gags.summary: Characters punctuate outrage at someone's behaviour with the rhetorical question 'What kind of a sick person would do a thing like that?'
phrases: what kind of a sick person
what kind of a sick woman
what kind of a sick lowlife

best.title: The Money
best.text: Mother's inventory of what Elaine brought: 'Vodka, cigarettes, fireworks.' Mother: 'What kind of a sick woman brings this to a 15-year-old?'

gags.name: opposite George / ignoring instincts
gags.summary: George discovers that doing the opposite of his every instinct leads to success, and the show returns to the comedy of him deliberately ignoring common sense.

best.title: The Opposite
best.text: A job with the New York Yankees! This has been the dream of my life ever since I was a child. It's all happening because I'm completely ignoring every urge towards common sense and good judgment I've ever had.

gags.name: borrowing money changes the relationship
gags.summary: Characters repeatedly invoke the idea that lending money to a friend is like having sex with them because it completely changes the relationship.
phrases: borrowing money from a friend is like having sex

best.title: The Calzone
best.text: And guess who's signed up for the truck? A free truck? Oh, boy, that completely changes our cost structure. Our G and A goes down 50 percent.

gags.name: 24 hours a day emanating sounds
gags.summary: Characters mock George's delusion that he is in his prime by cataloguing his physical failings, culminating in the line that 'all kinds of sounds are emanating from your body 24 hours a day'.
phrases: sounds are emanating from your body

best.title: The Boyfriend (1)
best.text: 'What do you have to do to become a buff?' / 'So Biff wants to be a buff? Well, sleeping less than 18 hours a day would be a start.'

gags.name: Cuban cigars confusion
gags.summary: Characters repeatedly confuse illegal Cuban cigars with Cuban people, and Kramer's schemes to obtain the contraband cigars keep resurfacing.

best.title: The English Patient
best.text: 'They're human beings from Cuba?' / 'I said Cubans. What did you think I meant?' / 'Cigars.' / 'Jerry, Cuban cigars are illegal in this country. That's why I got these guys.'

gags.name: good naked vs. bad naked
gags.summary: Characters debate that while nakedness sounds appealing in theory, certain activities make it unpleasant, distinguishing 'good naked' from 'bad naked'.

best.title: The Gymnast
best.text: I take it off when I go to the... You know, to the office. / What for? / Frees me up, no encumbrances. / Unbuttoned or all the way off? / All the way, baby.

gags.name: Louie's 'Crazy Lady'
gags.summary: Louie yells 'crazy lady' as an insult, often directed at his mother or female characters who annoy him.
phrases: keep your pants on, crazy lady

best.title: Substitute Father
best.text: Keep your pants on, crazy lady!

gags.name: Card Game in the Garage
gags.summary: The male drivers regularly gather to play cards in the garage, treating it as a serious and exclusive ritual that outsiders are shooed away from.
phrases: we're trying to play cards here
go play cards with the guys

best.title: Louies Mother
best.text: Jeff, you watch the cage for me here. I'm going to go play cards with the guys. I was invited.

gags.name: Will is from Philly
gags.summary: Will constantly drops references to growing up in Philly as a source of street-cred humor, often contrasting his old life with Bel-Air luxury.

best.title: Eye Tooth
best.text: Damn it, Jim. I'm a black boy from Philly, not a doctor.

gags.name: "I think I saw God"
gags.summary: Characters use the exaggerated claim of having seen God to describe an overwhelming or absurd experience for comic effect.

best.title: Mamas Baby Carltons Maybe
best.text: Carlton is the most incredible lover I have ever had... It was amazing, and endless, and magnificent. I think I saw God.

gags.name: "Now I know how" comparisons
gags.summary: Characters dramatically compare their current predicament to a famous figure or situation using "now I know how," played for comic self-pity.

best.title: Sleepless In Bel Air
best.text: Now I know how Captain Ahab felt when he was chasing Moby Dick. - Between the two of you, the cricket is the whale?

gags.name: Jheri curl jokes
gags.summary: Characters use the outdated Jheri curl hairstyle as a recurring punchline to signal that something or someone is hopelessly behind the times.

first.title: Aint No Business Like Show Business

best.title: The Client
best.text: Oh, and p.s... the Jheri curl played out with the jerk.

gags.name: Will's Whitney Houston obsession
gags.summary: Will is comically infatuated with Whitney Houston, referencing her in fantasies, owning a cardboard cutout of her, and daydreaming about her.

best.title: The Wedding Show Psyche
best.text: Just my luck...Whitney Houston and I had just survived a nuclear holocaust. And now I was the last man on Earth.

gags.name: 15 percent tip jokes
gags.summary: Characters repeatedly calculate or argue about tipping 15 percent, often as a punchline about cheapness or bad math.

best.title: A Decent Proposal
best.text: Well, now, just what exactly is 15 percent of a frozen burrito?

gags.name: Carlton mistaken for Bryant Gumbel
gags.summary: Carlton is repeatedly compared to or mistaken for news anchor Bryant Gumbel, mocking his stiff, assimilated demeanor.

best.title: The Fresh Prince Project
best.text: And Bryant Gumbel. He's darn good.

gags.name: Soul Train references
gags.summary: Characters repeatedly invoke Soul Train as a cultural touchstone for jokes about Black music, dancing, and street credibility.

best.title: 72 Hours
best.text: Man, y'all butchered that song. Hey, C, I'm telling you, if the Commodores heard you singing... they'd tie you down to the tracks and run you over with the soul train.

gags.name: "That's exactly why" put-downs
gags.summary: Characters use the phrase "that's exactly why" as a comic put-down structure to blame someone for an absurd consequence of their behavior.

first.title: Where Theres A Will Theres A Way 1

best.title: Where Theres A Will Theres A Way 1
best.text: See, that's exactly why fathers ain't allowed at the mall.

gags.name: Will's lucky drawers
gags.summary: Will repeatedly references a beloved pair of lucky underwear that he treats as a prized possession, played for absurdity each time.

best.title: Community Action
best.text: Jazz. I've had it with you, man! I'm about to... thank you for starching my lucky drawers.

gags.name: Hank's "Hey Now"
gags.summary: Hank's signature catchphrase, used as greeting, filler, and expression of delight, which the show repeatedly calls attention to as his defining, and hollow, trademark.

best.title: You're Having My Baby
best.text: After the big reveal: Hank takes back the 'Hey Now' button from Mary Beth.

gags.name: "Nothing to talk about" sign-off ritual
gags.summary: Artie closes out a smooth production day with a deadpan checklist, great show, glass of wine, masturbate, see you tomorrow, delivered as if reading a memo.
phrases: go home have a glass of wine

best.title: Artie's Gone
best.text: Have a glass of wine. / I'm not much of a drinker. / You don't have to drink it, Paula. Just walk in front of the audience with it. They see you're relaxed, it relaxes them.

gags.name: Hank's on-air emotional speech
gags.summary: Hank hijacks airtime for a seemingly heartfelt speech that inevitably pivots to self-promotion or is undercut by an absurd non-sequitur.

best.title: Hank's Divorce
best.text: ...that person has taught me about compassion, and that person has taught me about caring. And that person... is Mr. Larry Sanders. Give him a big hand.

gags.name: Hank's Look-Around Cafe
gags.summary: Hank repeatedly plugs his rotating restaurant venture on and off air, working it into unrelated conversations and offering tables to people who clearly don't want one.

best.title: The Grand Opening
best.text: Grand Opening of Hank's Look-Around Cafe, Friday night. Hank Kingsley, Proprietor.

gags.name: Hank's on-air disasters
gags.summary: Hank repeatedly does mortifying things live on air, proposing marriage, slurring a guest, falling, that blindside Larry and the crew.

best.title: Hank's Wedding
best.text: Hank proposes marriage on live television to a woman nobody on the show knew he was dating. Larry's stunned 'What?' captures his complete blindsiding.

gags.name: Phil's monologue jokes
gags.summary: The writing staff's debate over the quality of Phil's monologue jokes is a recurring beat, with Artie and Larry delivering backhanded assessments that keep Phil perpetually off-balance.

best.title: The Grand Opening
best.text: Hank: 'Like I've never laughed at your lame monologue jokes which I don't even get!'

gags.name: Olsen twins gag
gags.summary: The Olsen twins are dropped into unrelated conversations as a punchline about inappropriate or absurd celebrity fixation.

best.title: Where is the Love?
best.text: That's what the Olsen twins say.

gags.name: The weird intern
gags.summary: An unnamed, perpetually strange intern is casually delegated every unpleasant or bizarre task around the show, with other characters treating his weirdness as a known and exploitable resource.

best.title: The Grand Opening
best.text: the weird intern / We got one of those. / What's yours do? / He's just weird. That's exactly what ours does.

gags.name: Artie's "quite right" apology
gags.summary: Artie punctuates his own crude or offensive remarks with a stiff, mock-formal 'Quite right, inexcusable,' performing brief decorum before immediately reverting.

best.title: Larry Loses Interest
best.text: I'm afraid our boy is getting pussy-whipped. / Artie, ix-nay on the ussy-whipped-pay. / Quite right, Hank. Inexcusable. Forgive me, ladies.

gags.name: "Why don't we take a break"
gags.summary: Larry's reflexive escape hatch whenever an interview goes awkward or he blanks on a guest's credits, cutting to commercial instead of recovering.
phrases: why don't we take a break

best.title: The Matchmaker
best.text: Larry's on-air recovery: 'Well, then, what movie... I know you're great, and I'm a gigantic fan, and I saw you in, uh, this movie, uh... that... which movie am I thinking of? Which one? Well, why don't we take a break, and we'll come right back, and we'll figure out which movie I'm thinking of.'

gags.name: "No Flipping" sign-off
gags.summary: Larry ends every segment with an increasingly desperate plea for viewers not to change the channel during commercials.

best.title: Flip (2)
best.text: Larry's final sign-off: 'You may now flip.' — a callback to 'No flipping' throughout the show

gags.name: Jay Leno paranoia
gags.summary: Larry and the staff obsessively track Jay Leno as a rival and existential threat, with Larry repeatedly invoking how Leno displaced Carson as a warning about his own position.
phrases: that's what they did to johnny

best.title: Larry's New Love
best.text: sends his best. / That was my idea. / It's still good.

gags.name: "Better than last night's" crowd
gags.summary: Larry flatters each studio audience by telling them they are already so much better than the previous night's crowd, a hollow compliment the show keeps returning to.

best.title: The Warmth Episode
best.text: Well, you're no better than last night's audience. Thank you.

gags.name: Applause/Applesauce sign
gags.summary: Hank warms up the studio audience by squinting at the applause sign and pretending it reads 'applesauce,' then correcting himself, a bit he runs every show.
phrases: applesauce no i'm kidding it says applause

best.title: Being There
best.text: Hank misreads the 'applause' sign as 'applesauce' then immediately corrects himself

gags.name: Dwight's beet farm
gags.summary: Dwight's beet farm and his cousin Mose are a recurring source of absurd non-sequiturs and deadpan rural details.

best.title: Tallahassee
best.text: Dwight's pre-recorded memo to his son Philip: 'Philip, if you're hearing this memo, that can only mean one thing. I am dead. You are the rightful heir to Schrute Farms. Please, you must do one thing: Kill Mose before he kills you.'

gags.name: Andy went to Cornell
gags.summary: Andy repeatedly, unpromptedly volunteers that he went to Cornell, often with escalating self-congratulation.

best.title: The Job
best.text: Should not be a problem. I minored in history at the Ivy League school which I attended.

gags.name: Toby moving to Costa Rica
gags.summary: Toby repeatedly fantasizes about or announces he is moving to Costa Rica, never following through.

best.title: Branch Closing
best.text: Toby's closing confessional: 'For a minute there, I saw myself selling my house, moving to Costa Rica, learning how to surf. But Costa Rica will still be there when I'm 65.'

gags.name: Andy's anger management
gags.summary: Andy repeatedly references having completed anger management, usually while barely containing his anger.

best.title: Nepotism
best.text: Andy's anger management confessional: 'Am I angry that Gabe stole my girlfriend over the summer? No. I've been through anger management, okay? So right now I am sitting on a nice beach at Cape Cod, gazing out across the whitecaps. Oh, look, it's a humpback whale. How pretty. He's eating Gabe.'

gags.name: Dwight will tell on you
gags.summary: Dwight's go-to threat when he lacks real authority is to announce he will simply tell on the offender, playing his tattling like a deadly serious sanction.

best.title: Job Fair
best.text: Dwight: 'Or you will suffer the consequences.' 'What consequences?' 'I will tell on you.'

gags.name: Dwight hides behind pros and cons lists
gags.summary: Characters, especially Michael, produce absurd pros and cons lists whose entries reveal total irrationality rather than any genuine deliberation.

best.title: Casual Friday
best.text: Michael's pros and cons list for Ryan vs. Pam — Ryan's pros include 'I like his hair' and 'environmentally conscious because his mom drives him to work'

gags.name: Documentary crew awareness / nine years of filming
gags.summary: Characters in later seasons break the fourth wall to acknowledge they have been filmed for nine years, playing with the show's own meta-premise for laughs.

best.title: Finale
best.text: Pam, what was in the teapot letter? / I think I would rather keep that private. / If you've been filmed for nine years of your life, there'd be some things that you just want to keep to yourself. / I hear you. What did it say?

gags.name: Pam failed art school
gags.summary: Pam's failure at art school is used as a quick insult gag and also revisited as a quiet running thread about her creative ambitions.

best.title: Stress Relief
best.text: Individual 'Boom. Roasted.' insults — Jim: '6'11" and 90 pounds, Gumby has a better body.' / Dwight: 'you're a kiss-ass.' / Pam: 'you failed art school.' / Meredith: 'slept with so many guys you're starting to look like one.' / Kevin: 'I can't decide between a fat joke and a dumb joke.' / Creed: 'yo

gags.name: Michael is big picture only
gags.summary: Michael repeatedly declares himself a big-picture visionary who cannot be bothered with mundane day-to-day tasks like expense reports.

best.title: The Promotion
best.text: Michael: 'Gone with the Wind.' Employee: 'Never saw it.' Michael: 'Me neither. Chick flick.'

gags.name: Michael's ice cream cake obsession
gags.summary: Michael is irrationally devoted to ice cream cake at every office celebration, pushing for it regardless of allergies or occasion.

best.title: The Alliance
best.text: She's not the only one that's gonna be eating right? I think everybody likes ice cream cake

gags.name: Big Tuna
gags.summary: Andy nicknames Jim 'Big Tuna' after seeing him eat a tuna sandwich on his first day, and the name sticks among the Stamford/transferred employees.

best.title: Safety Training
best.text: Dwight's talking-head: 'I have decided to shun Andy Bernard for the next three years... I was shunned from the age of four until my sixth birthday for not saving the excess oil from a can of tuna.'

gags.name: Troy McClure's Introduction
gags.summary: Washed-up actor Troy McClure introduces himself by citing an absurd list of fake film and TV credits.
phrases: you may remember me from such
you might remember me from such

best.title: Barts Friend Falls In Love
best.text: Hello. I'm actor Troy McClure. You kids might remember me from such educational films as Lead Paint:: Delicious But Deadly and Here Comes The Metric System.

gags.name: "Sometimes I Wish" Dark Aside
gags.summary: A character voices a darkly comic or absurd wish that reveals their frustration, usually immediately undercut.

first.title: Bart Gets Hit By A Car

best.title: Holidays Of Future Passed
best.text: Sometimes I wish strangling your kid was still legal. Not since they passed Homer's Law.

gags.name: "You've Ruined" Accusation
gags.summary: A character dramatically accuses Homer or Bart of having ruined something, often escalating to an absurdly long list.

best.title: Bart Gets Famous
best.text: Damn TV! You've ruined my imagination just like you've ruined my ability to-- to, um-- uh-- Oh, well.

gags.name: "Now I Know How" Self-Pity
gags.summary: A character compares their minor predicament to that of a famous historical figure or deity for comic self-pity.
phrases: now i know how god feels

best.title: Bart Gets An F
best.text: Now I know how Washington felt when he surrendered Fort Necessity in 1754. You know, 1754. The famous defeat to the French.

gags.name: 742 Evergreen Terrace Address
gags.summary: The Simpsons' home address is repeatedly stated aloud in increasingly unlikely or comedic contexts.

best.title: Lisas Date With Density
best.text: If you can find it in your heart to forgive me... send one dollar to Sorry Dude, 742 Evergreen Terrace, Springfield.

gags.name: Budget Cuts Gag
gags.summary: Springfield's perpetual budget cuts are cited as the absurd reason for ridiculous school or civic cost-saving measures.

best.title: My Mother The Carjacker
best.text: Due to budget cuts, music class will now have a two drink minimum.

gags.name: Homer's "I'll Teach You" Threat
gags.summary: Homer begins an angry threat with 'I'll teach you to…' but the phrasing accidentally implies he wants to teach the behaviour, not punish it.

best.title: Home Sweet Homediddly Dum Doodily
best.text: Lousy house plant! You son of a- I'll teach you to- D'oh-You-

gags.name: Bart's Ay Caramba
gags.summary: Bart's catchphrase of shock or surprise, uttered when he sees something alarming or outrageous.

best.title: The Father The Son And The Holy Guest St
best.text: Ay caramba, do the Bartman, etcetera, etcetera.

gags.name: Bart's Eat My Shorts
gags.summary: Bart's dismissive catchphrase used to tell someone to get lost or leave him alone.

best.title: The Fat And The Furriest
best.text: And then finally, I can eat my shorts!

gags.name: Ned Flanders's Okilly-Dokilly
gags.summary: Ned Flanders's cheerful, folksy catchphrase used as an affirmative response.

best.title: Two Bad Neighbors
best.text: Tiptop-notch! - Okilly-dokilly. Thankilly-dankilly. - Greatalicious. - Scrumpdiddlerific. Fine and dandy like sour candy!

gags.name: Bart's Prank Calls to Moe
gags.summary: Bart phones Moe's Tavern and asks for a fake name that sounds like an insult when Moe shouts it to the bar.

best.title: Moena Lisa
best.text: Screw you, snail trail! Who was that? Eh, some jerk making a prank call with a gag name: 'Tom Wolfe.'

gags.name: Homer's D'oh
gags.summary: Homer's signature grunt of frustration, used whenever something goes wrong for him.

first.title: Simpsons Roasting On An Open Fire

best.title: Bart Gets Famous
best.text: You'll always have them to remind you of the time when you were the whole world's special little guy. Thanks, Mom. And now you can go back to just being you instead of a one-dimensional character with a silly catchphrase. D'oh! Ay, caramba! Hidilly-ho! Ha-ha! Excellent.

gags.name: "I cannot stand"
gags.summary: Characters declare they 'cannot stand' something with mock dignity, used as a running comic device to reveal petty or hypocritical pet peeves.

best.title: Debate
best.text: If there's any dirty trick that I cannot stand, it is honesty.

gags.name: "Are you fucking kidding me"
gags.summary: Characters respond to outrageous plot developments or admissions with 'are you fucking kidding me', a repeated punchline reaction shot of disbelief.

best.title: Oslo
best.text: You can have Tibet. / What? / Yeah. You can have Tibet back. Are you fucking kidding me? / No. Right after the election, you can have it back.

gags.name: "God Almighty"
gags.summary: Characters punctuate moments of absurdity or horror with 'God Almighty' as a comic exclamation, often followed by a devastating comparison or non-sequitur.

best.title: Clovis
best.text: Jonah with money. God Almighty. It's like if Hitler could fly.

gags.name: "I'll tell you something"
gags.summary: Selina prefaces darkly comic or self-revealing confessions with 'I'll tell you something', treating the phrase as a rhetorical wind-up to an outrageous punchline.

best.title: Judge
best.text: I'll tell you something, if I had a crib for every baby who died inside me, I could open up a Pottery Barn Kids.

gags.name: "Shut the fuck up"
gags.summary: Characters, most often Selina or her staff, deploy 'shut the fuck up' as a punchline deflation after someone says something oblivious or sycophantic, often immediately following a compliment.

best.title: C**tgate
best.text: From now on, Jonah, you will shut the fuck up and do exactly as I say. And if you listen to me instead of your only two brain cells busy butt-fucking each other somewhere in the vast expanses of your misshapen skull, then maybe, Jonah, you might have a chance at becoming the first mentally impaired

gags.name: "Jesus fucking Christ"
gags.summary: Selina and others use increasingly elaborate invocations of Jesus Christ as an expletive of exasperation, often triggered by spectacular incompetence.

best.title: Special Relationship
best.text: I couldn't help but overhear, but I always thought that lady was a little damaged. / Jesus fucking Christ. You're fired.

gags.name: Drone strike casual mentions
gags.summary: Drone strikes are casually referenced as an everyday administrative tool, played for dark comedy by treating extrajudicial killing as a mundane bureaucratic footnote.

best.title: South Carolina
best.text: Thank you, ma'am. I learned from an Afghani warlord. / We should put him on the payroll. / You killed him in a drone strike. / Oh, well.

gags.name: "Why / How / Where the fuck"
gags.summary: Characters punctuate bafflement or frustration by inserting 'the fuck' into question words, a recurring verbal tic used for comic emphasis throughout the series.

best.title: Clovis
best.text: Everybody who said that I would never make it... where the fuck are you now, huh? / Some of them are still in senior positions.

gags.name: "Stupid fucking" compound insults
gags.summary: Characters, especially Selina, construct elaborately contemptuous compound insults using 'stupid fucking' as a building block, often delivered while publicly smiling.

best.title: Andrew
best.text: Selina learning Andrew's PAC funded both sides: 'I just was fluffed and then I got fucked.' — and then: 'Do you know-- smile. Smile, you stupid asshole. Make it bigger.'

gags.name: "In your fucking face" / "fucking face"
gags.summary: The phrase 'fucking face' recurs in colourful threats and insults, most memorably Selina declaring she'd rather be shot in the face than be VP again.

best.title: Fishing
best.text: Selina: 'I'd rather be shot in the fucking face than serve as vice president again. Seriously, in the fucking face!'

gags.name: "Would like to say a few words" (Gary)
gags.summary: The show repeatedly sets up Gary to be invited to say a few words in front of a group, playing on his devotion to Selina and his comic inability or refusal to speak publicly.

best.title: Judge
best.text: And I think the birthday boy would like to say a few words. / Would you like to say a few words, Gar? / Gary, you wanna come up? / No.

gags.name: "Might add" parenthetical asides
gags.summary: Characters, especially Selina, tack on 'I might add' to inject passive-aggressive editorial asides into otherwise neutral statements, as a recurring verbal comedy tic.

best.title: Blurb
best.text: If Jackie Kennedy can go through the day with her husband's philandering brains all over her dress and her head held high... even though they made her ride around in a convertible like an animal, I might add...

gags.name: Insulting the American people
gags.summary: Characters invoke 'the American people' in ways that inadvertently or deliberately reveal contempt for ordinary voters while ostensibly claiming to serve them.

best.title: Library
best.text: If only the American people could've known you for your sense of humor instead of your bizarre indifference to apartheid.

gags.name: Setting fire / fire metaphors
gags.summary: Characters repeatedly use 'set fire' as a vivid metaphor for self-sabotage or escalating crises, often in elaborate extended analogies about political disasters.

best.title: Fundraiser
best.text: What the fuck, Amy? / I am putting out two fires in there, and I turn around to find out that you have set fire to the fucking fire truck.

gags.name: Nobel Peace Prize obsession
gags.summary: Selina repeatedly fantasises about and demands a Nobel Peace Prize, treating it as a personal entitlement and running joke about her delusions of grandeur.

best.title: Oslo
best.text: All the time. Aung San Suu Kyi, Henry Kissinger, and also, the prize that you're getting, it is not the Peace Prize. / Oh, don't start with that! / It is a second-tier Peace Prize. / No. / It is made of very hard plastic.
